fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Chewing the cud is only half of it. The text says, “The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:4) One sign by itself doesn't get an animal on the list. I once tried to bake with only the chocolate chips and called it a batch. The oven was not impressed.
Grass is a fair guess, friend, but the verse never mentions it. What it says is that the pig “does not chew the cud.” (Leviticus 11:7) The word you want is cud. That's the sign the pig is missing.

True. God says, “You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:8) So the command covers touching the carcasses as well as eating the meat. Keep that in your pocket, because the passage comes back to touching carcasses later.

Yes, hopping. The exception is for flying insects “…having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.” (Leviticus 11:21) Verse 22 then names the kinds: locust, katydid, cricket and grasshopper. The text gives the legs and the names together, friend.
